'''Mie ayam''', '''mi ayam''', or '''bakmi ayam''' ([[Indonesian language|Indonesian]] for '[[Chicken as food|chicken]] [[bakmi]]', literally 'chicken noodles') is a common [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian]] dish of seasoned yellow wheat [[noodle]]s topped with diced [[Chicken as food|chicken meat]] (''[[wikt:ayam#Indonesian|ayam]]'').<ref>{{cite web | title = Chicken Noodles / Mie Ayam | author = Marvellina | work = What to Cook Today | url = http://whattocooktoday.com/chicken-noodles-mie-ayam.html | access-date = 2016-02-15 | archive-date = 2016-02-23 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160223043359/http://whattocooktoday.com/chicken-noodles-mie-ayam.html | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | title = Noodle! 100 Amazing Authentic Recipes | author = MiMi Aye | publisher = A&C Black | year = 2014 | isbn = 9781472910615 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=gdrHAwAAQBAJ&q=bakmi+ayam+Chinese+Indonesian+noodle&pg=PA105 | page = 105 | access-date = 15 February 2016}}</ref> It is derived from culinary techniques employed in [[Chinese cuisine]].<ref name="Von Holzen">{{cite book | title = A New Approach to Indonesian Cooking | author = Heinz Von Holzen | publisher = Marshall Cavendish International Asia Pte Ltd | year = 2014 | isbn = 9789814634953 | page = 15 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=pRuiBQAAQBAJ&q=mie+ayam+Chinese+Indonesian+chicken+noodle&pg=PA15 | access-date = 15 February 2016 }}</ref><ref name="EbrahimYee2006">{{cite book|author1=Geok Boi Lee|title=Classic Asian Noodles|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TsCV6YZXPQoC&q=history+of+noodles+in+southeast+asia&pg=PA2|year=2007|publisher=Marshall Cavendish|isbn=978-981-232-922-6|pages=47–48}}</ref> In Indonesia, the dish is recognized as a popular [[Chinese Indonesian cuisine|Chinese Indonesian dish]],<ref name="Von Holzen"/> served by restaurants, street-side ''[[warung]]'', and travelling vendor carts frequenting residential areas.
